description: The plot illustrates how loss varies with computation cost (TFLOPs) for two training setups, shown as two line series with markers and a legend. The x-axis is labeled “TFLOPs,” uses a linear scale, and runs from 0.00 to 1.25 with an axis multiplier of 1e9 indicated (i.e., values are shown in billions of TFLOPs), with regularly spaced tick labels every 0.25. The y-axis is labeled “Loss,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 2.40 to 2.75 with tick labels at about 0.05 intervals. The “Vanilla” series is drawn as a purple solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers; it starts near the left edge around loss ≈2.75 at roughly 0.05×1e9 TFLOPs and then decreases gradually across the axis, reaching about 2.60 around 0.30×1e9 and ending near 2.50 at about 1.20×1e9 TFLOPs. The “SepLLM” series is drawn as a red solid line with circular markers; it begins near loss ≈2.74 at roughly 0.05×1e9 TFLOPs, drops to around 2.60 by about 0.25×1e9, continues downward past ≈2.54 near 0.50×1e9, reaches roughly 2.50 around 0.95×1e9, and ends near 2.47 at about 1.20×1e9 TFLOPs. A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at loss = 2.50, and green dashed vertical lines and a double-headed arrow annotate an interval on the right side of the plot labeled “1.28×,” spanning from roughly 0.95×1e9 to about 1.23×1e9 TFLOPs.
